patient_information: A previously healthy 20-year-old man from southern India.
history_of_present_illness: He had fever for 4 days, followed by tingling and weakness initially in his left leg, subsequently involving all four limbs over the next 2 days. After admission, he developed autonomic instability, dysphagia, and respiratory distress.
exposure_and_epidemiology: He has a history of a stray dog bite (WHO category III) on his left lower limb 1 month before symptom onset in a rabies-endemic country. He received five doses of anti-rabies vaccine but no rabies immunoglobulin.
vitals: Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, pulse 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate 26 breaths per minute, and temperature 38.5°C (101.3°F).
physical_exam: On admission, he is conscious with normal mental functions (GCS 15/15). Neurological examination revealed a flaccid, areflexic quadriparesis.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood investigations, including serum electrolytes, renal, and liver function tests, were normal. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) showed 52 mg/dL protein (reference: 15–50mg/dL), 60 mg/dL glucose (reference: 50–75mg), and 340 cells/mm³ (60% polymorphs, 40% lymphocytes; normal ≤5 cells/mm³). His saliva sample collected at admission was positive for rabies viral RNA by RT-PCR; a CSF sample was negative.
differential_diagnosis: Guillain Barré Syndrome, Post-vaccination encephalomyelitis, NMDAR antibody-mediated/Autoimmune encephalitis, Campylobacter-associated summer paralysis syndrome, Cerebral malaria, Herpes simplex encephalitis, Arthropod-borne encephalitides (e.g. Japanese encephalitis, West Nile Virus encephalitis, etc.), Poliomyelitis, B-virus (Cercopithecine herpesvirus 1) encephalomyelitis, Tetanus, Snake- or Scorpion-envenomation, Organophosphate poisoning, Illicit drug use, CNS intoxicants, Psychiatric disorders.
management_and_clinical_course: Management consisted of symptomatic treatment and supportive care. He required mechanical ventilation on the third day after hospitalization due to dysphagia and respiratory distress. The patient died of a sudden cardiac arrest on the fifth day of hospitalization (9 days post-onset of symptoms).

Full thickness biopsy and adequate hair follicles required
